note: What has been improved in the atlas, newest first, one plain headline each. Hand-written, because a changelog read off the commit log says what a developer did and not what a reader can now do. The home page shows the latest four and /whats-new/ shows all of them. Add an entry when a change a visitor can see goes live, not when it is merged. date is YYYY-MM-DD; href is a path inside the atlas (starting with /) or omitted.

entries.headline: Loading screen: leaves drift down from the tree, and a seed drops, takes root and grows into a small plant
entries.what: While a family tree file is read, the animated tree now lets a couple of leaves fall to the ground, and a seed drops, takes root beside the trunk and grows into a small plant. It is only a picture: nothing from your file is used.
entries.how: Asked for by the owner after watching the loading animation.

entries.headline: Draw-an-area panel says what the Add button adds (books and archives, not places); archive links open in a new tab
entries.what: After you draw an area on the map, the panel counted places (178) but its button counted books and archives (500 of 656), which read as a contradiction. It now says what the button adds, lists the books in each place, and opens archive pages in a new tab so your drawn areas stay on the map.
entries.how: Spotted by the owner while drawing areas on the map.

entries.headline: Tree Canvas opening screen: far shorter, with one drop zone, one link row and a row of chips
entries.what: The first screen of the Tree Canvas was about two screens of explanation. It is now one drop zone, one row for a link, a row of chips for the family archives, and a slim line for keeping your work. The explanations moved into tooltips and the About fold.
entries.how: The owner found it too long and too wordy.

entries.headline: Tree Canvas: two more Views, Night sky (your chosen people as stars, with a Play through the years) and Place lanes
entries.what: Night sky shows the people you chose as stars on a dark sky, by side of the family or by place, with a Play through the years. Place lanes gives one row for each place, with who ruled it behind it and a table of who ruled each place.

entries.headline: Tree Canvas: two new Views, Generations (parents back, children forward) and Household (a family along a timeline)
entries.what: Generations shows parents back to great-grandparents and children forward, with how related each is. Household shows parents, brothers and sisters, partners and children along a timeline of years.

entries.headline: Tree Canvas: the dotted "not graded" lines are now real, bolder dots instead of faint ticks
entries.what: The dotted lines that mean 'not graded' (a link no archive has graded; not proof and not doubt) were drawn as hairline ticks. They are now round dots, thicker and further apart.
entries.how: The owner found the dotted lines too faint.

entries.headline: Connect: the seven doors sit on one row with icons, and every code block has a copy button
entries.what: The seven 'Pick your door' tiles on the Connect page now sit on one row with an icon each, and every code block has a small copy button. In the Croatia walk-through the button copies only the curl line.

entries.headline: Roots & Routes Orphans: families under an Unknown parent are no longer "detached" (521 people in 103 was really 36 in 6)
entries.what: The Orphans view counted anyone whose parent was an 'Unknown' placeholder as detached. A family that hangs off an Unknown parent is now counted in its whole group: on a real file, 521 people in 103 groups turned out to be 36 people in 6.
entries.how: Found when the owner's own tree showed hundreds of people as detached; checked against that real file.

entries.headline: Roots & Routes: click anyone under "Not drawn yet" for their panel, relatives and where to look
entries.what: Under 'Not drawn yet' the names did nothing when clicked. Each is now a button that opens the person's panel, with their relatives and where to look (the archive or tree they came from).
entries.how: The owner clicked a name under 'Not drawn yet' and nothing happened.

entries.headline: Connect page: a Croatia walk-through from "which archives?" to eras and flags, with every address and its output
entries.what: A worked example on the Connect page: want data for a country, find it, and list the end points and data examples and formats. Seven steps for Croatia, each with its address, a real captured answer and what the format means.

entries.headline: Compare: "+N beyond" and "Walk from here" restart the comparison at that person, with Back to return and pairings kept
entries.what: In Compare mode you could not go further up or down the tree, unlike the other views. 'Walk from here' now restarts the comparison at any person, with a Back button to return and your accepted pairings kept.
entries.how: The owner asked why Compare could not be navigated up and down.

entries.headline: Three more files now have addresses: place names by year, 969 contributed collections (CC0), FamilySearch collections
entries.what: Place names by year, the 969 contributed collections (CC0) and FamilySearch collections each now have a plain web address that returns the whole file, with the curl line to fetch it.

links.t: Every file, and its curl line

entries.how: Read from Wiktionary and Wikipedia pages, each form carrying its source. See the line 'forms of given names added' for the list.

links.t: Every file, and its curl line

entries.headline: Norwegian surnames: 44 families, Olsen to Åsen, with -sen, -søn, -son, -datter and Aa/Å forms
entries.what: 44 Norwegian surname families, from Olsen to Åsen, with the -sen, -søn, -son and -datter endings and the Aa/Å spellings treated as the same name.
entries.how: Built from rules (Wikipedia's pages on patronymics and Norwegian orthography), not from records. See the line 'spellings of 44 surnames' for the list.

My research map: finished places are ticked, and the next neighbouring places with FamilySearch books form a path
My research: a book's note no longer repeats itself dozens of times; old repeats are cleaned up when the page opens
Marking pages or a note with no family chosen now asks whose research it is, instead of dropping what you typed
301 more sources have their cost to look worked out, and 9 national or territorial archives were added
Place pages list each book once: the two volume sections are merged, with cost, film and denomination on one row
Type a place on the sources page (Durban, Fiume, Senj) and see the archives that cover it, its country's, and its region
Source counts moved to the home screen's metrics board; New, Help check and About are small icons beside the search
Whose archive (record regions and eras) is now a second view on the sources page, searched from the same box
One sources page: search, filter by country or cost, see new sources, help check one. Survey a source is now part of it
A Sources button at the top right of every page opens a search over every archive, library and portal listed
A file kept on this device now opens straight on its Fix list; a separate Tree button opens it on the tree
On the Roots & Routes fix list, sections and groups with nothing left to do are greyed out and ticked
Searching a two-word country such as South Africa now narrows "Whose flag flew there"; the South African flag is fixed
Roots & Routes shows your saved fix list on its first screen, linked to My research, with no GEDCOM needed
Place pages open with a summary: its country, that country's flags and sources, and the flags that flew over it
Stories read untidy writing: no capitals, texting, a father's father and his wife in one sentence
Roots & Routes: Places to review shows its list again, the Fix list tab has a count, and the save buttons sit in one row
Story place cards show the names a place was filed under, with years, and links to its page, country, flags and region
Stories find a place by its old name: Fiume is Rijeka, Pola is Pula, Laibach is Ljubljana, and "Rhodesia" picks Harare
Stories: "Add this family to your research" sits under the heading, and a story can join a family you already have
On a phone the Researching family picker is in the menu, not lost; stories offer "did you mean" for misspelt places
Stories keep the person: looks, loves, marriages, hard times, weather and how they died, as told, never as fact
Stories: no places from words like "young" or "miner", trades kept, and "my father Marco" and "married Anna" read
Stories read more truthfully: countries, years by place, a named wife, flags on every place, and the Second World War
My story starts like the map: add photos, read them with Claude, try an example, see what the Atlas understood
My research has an Other names tab: every other name in the same family session, and the intro lists every country
My research no longer carries a "Written elsewhere" tab; it shows only the family you are working on
My research now opens with a short introduction to the name: where it is counted, and whose flag flew there.
The Flags Atlas pages use the full page width of the rest of the site, with text kept to a readable line
The Places menu is short again: one row opens the hubs, instead of listing all 34.
Connection & Backup has real icons: browser, file, cloud and share, and on the back-up, import, send and link buttons
Who are you looking for? is simpler: write a few words, add a photo, and Claude reads it only when you press the button.
My research is titled with the family, shows its research session, and has Rename, Remove and Print / save as PDF
The volume count is now an icon with Save, Read and Contrast. It pulses when there is news or the Atlas has grown.
The Local dot is now a save button beside Read and Contrast: orange and pulsing when saved only here, green when online.
Relatives from one village share one card, with only the wars of their own years, and nearby books if it has none.
The volume count now sits right of Local in the header, in short form (3.43M).
Add pictures to a story and press Read: what they say joins the story, and the pictures stay with it in this browser.
Views and Filters are now just icons on the search line. The funnel fills in colour when you have changed a filter.
Looking for someone? A story that gives his father and mother draws both on the tree, and no longer puts you in it.
One search box for a place, a surname or a family story, with live pills. No family is chosen for you in My research.
Their journey now shows each year's flag, epidemics, wars and famines nearby, who led, and how the names were written.
The home map now has Start with your story: type or drop a photo, watch the journey draw, then start the family.
Reading the record now opens with a guided walk-through: what you have, what you know, their journey, your first steps.
New: say who you are looking for in one sentence, then see their journey on the map and a plan of what to look at first.
My research is now in tabs and lists the GEDCOM fixes still to do; the Ask page on Reading the record is simpler.
Roots & Routes now keeps your last tree files in this browser only; reopen one with a click, or untick to keep nothing.
Documents you read now get an Atlas page: a grey map, who held each place, registers, sources and name variants.
Read forms and certificates as whole documents, compare them in a case file, and save it all with the pictures.
Your online copy now saves itself on every page, a few seconds after a change, with no button to press.
Record Reader takes up to four pictures, then hands the reading over as a PDF, a text file and a prompt.
Reading old records has its own button, and now tells the story of a line: the place, its flag, its volumes and a map.
One search finds a country's records, its flag history and its hub, and the places menu now holds the flags.
Draw several areas and save them as one named group, or save the map as a view. Both sit in Views beside the search box.
entries.tip: Views: your saved map views and named areas.

entries.headline: Your saved areas, views and the names of your GEDCOM files now travel with your research, in the file and the six words.
entries.tip: This card lists everything kept with your research.

entries.headline: Light and dark mode: the sun and moon button at the end of the menu switches, and the atlas remembers it.
Connection & Backup shows the days since your last sync and your last file backup, with the date.
Some What's new lines now take you to the exact button they describe and point at it with a speech bubble.
A My research switch colours the map by what you have researched, so you can see what is done. It now lives in Filters.
Draw a box or shape on the map to list the places, books and archives inside, coloured by your research, then add them.
entries.tip: Draw a box or a shape here, then see what lies inside it.

entries.headline: Colour the map by your research: researched, busy researching, on my list, not started. Switch it on in Filters.
entries.tip: Open Filters: My research is at the top.

entries.headline: The Filters button is bigger and its panel roomier, with clearer groups.
entries.tip: The Filters button, bigger, with a roomier panel.

entries.headline: About now holds the sources too, in a two-level menu; the volume count sits beside the logo.
entries.tip: Open About: What's new and The sources are here now.

entries.headline: Mass-mortality events are equal-size cards with a short line each; the play control is at the map's bottom left.
Home counts now include the 5,943 eras tracked, and flags agree: 211 countries, 34 hubs.
entries.tip: Open the volume count to see eras, flags and hubs.

entries.headline: Volumes are listed once per place, and the book list sits inside the FamilySearch column.
Connection & Backup page: green dot online, orange local, red offline, and a warning if changes sit unsaved a day.
entries.tip: Your connection and backup status, with days since the last sync.

entries.headline: Reloading a place link opens that place; each volume is listed once; My research uses the full width.
A What's new button in the header, one volumes pill that opens the inventory, and a phone layout that fits the screen.
A surname's origin is now one compact card, and the header shows a green Live or red Offline dot.
My research can now save a dated backup file, restore one, and share a pack of what you found with someone else.
Reading old records: look up a Latin word from a register, and decode a date like die 30 7bris 1671
Names: type your whole name (David Ivan Defranceski) and every part is searched at once, given names paired by language
Name pages: who carried the name, by century and state, from Wikidata (the dead only), piloted on 20 names
Archive lists: the access colour is now on the number and its map pin, with no dot line, and rows alternate in tint
Place panel: FamilySearch volumes join their column, every list folds, the header is one row and names whose finds
Names: a page for every given name, with where it is said to come from, and two sourced stories of names on the move
Sources: each country now has one sources page, and place pages link to it instead of repeating the list
Names: a spelling shows under every language that writes it; Croatian, Serbian and Slovene forms added
Given names: the catalogue grew from 89 to 630 names (5,323 forms in 49 languages), each form with its source
Place panel: one sources block with the verdict, your progress, your archives and everywhere else
Roots & Routes fix list: grouped by what to do, with the Atlas's records, rulers and flags under each row, and a PDF
Greenland: 18 parishes and 118 church-ledger volumes from the National Archives, with the ones held offline marked
Roots & Routes: animated views, where to look for what is missing, and the old name of each place (Fiume, Salisbury)
Say your name: every form of a given name or a surname, and which ones a register has shown
277 wars, uprisings and massacres of 20,000+ dead on the map, with sources and where to find their dead
Zimbabwe's flag history now shows the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland, 1953 to 1963
Wars, famines, genocides and epidemics, from the Holocaust to the Croatian war, now list where to find their dead
994 record regions now show who held the ground, era by era, across Africa, Asia and beyond
Places outside a record region now show each era's leader and system
Surname spellings: one catalogue, with the evidence for each
The home page no longer freezes browsers: map layers load when you switch them on
Add a source: a tidier form, and a header button that no longer squashes
A new source: UK Genealogy Archives, with free census, parish-register and marriage transcripts
History: 94 more movements now go somewhere on the map
History on a phone: year and era share a row, and the search is slimmer
Mass mortality on the map: 75 epidemics, famines, massacres and sieges, with what the sources say
History: focus on one country and watch only its movements and the flags it flew
Full screen is a button on the map, under the zoom controls
